contributions.statement: Keep durable coding preferences in committed, reviewed files rather than opaque host memory, because a single stored insecure preference raised vulnerability rates 2.7-50.3 pp while models disclosed the memory's influence in only 2-10% of responses.
contributions.evidence: §6.1 Table 2 and §6.2.1 (kappa 0.97-0.98): four assistants, Python and JS/C/C++/Go. The memory was task-targeted (best case for the attack), and these are chat assistants, not coding-agent hosts.
relative_to: memory poisoning attacks on LLM agents

contributions.statement: When adding security requirements to agent prompts, track functional pass rate alongside vulnerability rate, because appending them cut vulnerabilities 19.7-33.6 pp but cut ChatGPT's pass rate by 15.9 pp.
contributions.evidence: §6.4 Table 7 on 28-29 prompts, two systems; Gemini's pass loss was only 6.0 pp, so the cost is model-dependent.

reason: Gives measured magnitudes for silent preference carry-over and for the security/functionality trade-off of security prompts; the 100% memory-filter result is recall-only and excluded.
